paper_metadata.title: Quantum Optimization for Portfolio Management in Financial Services Using the Variational Quantum Eigensolver (VQE) Algorithm

experiments.description: Hybrid VQE-based portfolio optimization evaluated on a 20-asset portfolio and compared against classical mean-variance optimization and Black-Litterman baseline models.

hyperparameters.objective_tradeoff: minimize risk and maximize expected return

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Portfolio weights are represented as coefficients in the quantum circuit; the portfolio objective is cast as a Hamiltonian.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Minimize H(w) = alpha * (w^T Sigma w) - beta * (w^T r), balancing portfolio variance and expected return.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Not specified beyond the portfolio optimization formulation; mentions transaction cost, liquidity, and regulatory constraints in the general problem statement.
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: H(w) = alpha * w^T Sigma w - beta * w^T r

problem_instance.description: Portfolio optimization on a sample set of twenty stocks.
problem_instance.dataset_name: Yahoo Finance / Quandl / Bloomberg (candidate sources mentioned)

dataset_specification.description: Historical stock price data; daily closing prices over 5-10 years; focus on 20-50 most liquid shares across 50 sectors; exact ticker symbols and date range not reported.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Compute average expected return, variance/covariance matrix, volatility, Value at Risk, and alphas from historical prices; incorporate transaction cost, risk tolerance, and liquidity characteristics.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Comparison against classical MVO and Black-Litterman using portfolio risk (variance), expected return, Sharpe ratio, and convergence time.

noise_model.noise_type: decoherence mentioned in general; no explicit noise model specified

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Historical market data collection; compute returns, covariance matrix, volatility, VaR, and alpha; formulate classical mean-variance baseline.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Evaluate portfolio risk, expected return, Sharpe ratio, and convergence time; compare with MVO and Black-Litterman.

speedup_claims.conditions: For the reported 20-asset instance, VQE converged in 120 s versus 15 s for MVO.
speedup_claims.caveats: VQE is slower than the classical baseline on the tested problem size; the paper speculates that quantum advantage may emerge for larger portfolios, but no larger-size timing results are reported.

speedup_claims.conditions: For the reported 20-asset instance, VQE converged in 120 s versus 25 s for BLM.
speedup_claims.caveats: VQE is slower than BLM on the tested instance; the paper claims scalability benefits for larger problems without providing empirical evidence.

speedup_claims.factor: potential advantage for large-scale portfolio optimization
speedup_claims.conditions: As problem size increases and quantum hardware improves
speedup_claims.caveats: This is a qualitative claim only; no asymptotic complexity or crossover point is provided.
